name: First Bulgarian Empire
summary: A medieval Balkan state founded by the Bulgars under Asparuh. In the 9th–10th centuries it rivalled Byzantium and became a centre of Slavic Christian culture and the Cyrillic script.

location.value: South-eastern Europe; at its height from the Danube Bend to the Black Sea and from the Dnieper to the Adriatic.

terrain.value: The lower Danube plain, the Balkan Mountains and Macedonia.

climate.value: Continental, with cold winters north of the Balkan Mountains.

resources.value: Farmland in the Danube plain, pasture for horses and sheep, and salt.

disasters.value: Unknown in detail; Byzantine sources mention famines.

population.value: No reliable estimate; perhaps a few million under Simeon.

urbanisation.value: Capitals Pliska and Preslav, later Ohrid.

migration.value: Bulgars led by Asparuh moved south of the Danube and joined with South Slavs.

economicBase.value: Farming and herding; trade with Byzantium.

tradeRoutes.value: Trade along the Danube and the Black Sea; a trade treaty with Byzantium (716).

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.

moneyAndTax.value: Used Byzantine coins; collected tribute from Byzantium at times.

governmentType.value: A monarchy led by a khan, then by a tsar (emperor) from Simeon’s time (913).

keyRulers.value: Asparuh (founder), Krum, Boris I (converted, 864), Simeon I the Great (893–927), Samuel.

succession.value: Hereditary within the ruling dynasty, though rivals sometimes seized power.

institutions.value: A Byzantine-style church and court; a Bulgarian patriarchate (recognised 927).

stability.value: Civil strife and invasions followed the death of Simeon (927).

eliteConflict.value: Boyars (nobles) revolted against Boris I’s conversion to Christianity (866).

armyAndTech.value: Strong cavalry and fortresses; Krum used siege engines against Constantinople.

majorWars.value: Long wars with Byzantium; Battle of Kleidion (1014).

territoryChange.value: At its height a major power able to compete with Byzantium.

alliancesRivals.value: Rival of Byzantium; contacts with the Franks.

inventions.value: Little is known; the Cyrillic script was developed in its schools.

scienceEducation.value: Literary schools of Preslav and Ohrid developed Old Church Slavonic literature.

openness.value: Adopted Byzantine Christianity (864) but kept its own Slavonic church language.

communicationTransport.value: Roman roads through the Balkans; boats on the Danube.

languageWriting.value: Old Church Slavonic; the Cyrillic script developed here.

artsArchitecture.value: The Madara Rider rock relief and churches of Preslav.

socialStructure.value: Tsar, boyars, clergy, free farmers and dependent peasants.

dailyLife.value: Wooden and earth houses in villages; stone palaces in Pliska and Preslav; bread, meat and dairy.

neighbours.value: Byzantium, the Franks, Magyars, Kievan Rus’.

ideasReligions.value: Spread Slavic Christian books to Serbia and Rus’.

riseSignals.value: Founded 680–681 after defeating a Byzantine army.

peakPeriod.value: The 9th and 10th centuries, under Simeon I.

declineSignals.value: Invasions by the Rus’ (968–971) and Byzantine wars under Basil II.

outcome.value: Conquered by Byzantium under Basil II in 1018.

sources.value: Byzantine chronicles and inscriptions. Checked against Wikipedia (“First Bulgarian Empire”).
